source: strings QA round 2 (2026-09-25 ~01:10); strings fix r2 was killed by the session limit mid-way (its WIP is commit 9ec1a38)

defects.issue: Some built sustain samples dip and jump back in their first second, so certain held notes wobble 6-7.5 dB. This is the same size and sound as the round-1 interference defect, but it comes from the samples, not from layer mixing. Every long violin I Eb5 in the test music does it.
defects.evidence: qa/round2/results/samples_shape.json: 69 of 1094 normal/legato regions start low, dip 5.5-17 dB and recover within the first 1.2 s. violin_mf_075_Eb5.wav (both offsets) sits about 3 dB low, drops to -6 dB re steady at 0.5-0.65 s, then jumps +5.7 dB. violin2 pp legato D4 (62): -7.7 dB at 0.2 s, +6.2 dB. Unused by SK_final but worse: vn1/vn2 pp 99 (-16.9 dB), va pp 91/80/89/93 (-9 to -12 dB, +10-12 dB jumps). held_sk_final.json: vn1's six worst long notes are all Eb5 (6.65-7.5 dB p2-p98 after removing the requested CC1/CC11 level; vn1 p90 over 63 long notes 6.6 dB); vn2's two worst are D4 (6.25 and 5.84 dB). The edge A/B (CC1 71->72) leaves the Eb5 wobble at 6.9 dB, so layer mixing is not the cause. 18 of SK_final's notes of 0.5 s or longer land on flagged regions (vn1 14, vn2 4). NORMAL_RISE's steady-3 dB test is fooled by the low plateau before the notch.
defects.fix: In iowa_build.py, at build time, measure each normal and legato region's 50 ms level from its offset (an_samples.shape: early_db <= -3, or notch <= -5.5 dB with a >= 4.5 dB jump). Then either move the offset past the recovery (the first point after which the level stays within +-2 dB of steady), or flatten the first 1.2 s with a slow gain correction to the steady level (the way attack_tune flattens pitch). Add the criterion to setup_strings.sh's verification gate and re-run an_samples.py and an_held.py; the target is vn1 Eb5 at or below 3 dB p2-p98.

defects.issue: --wet -4 is 'reverb 4 dB under the dry sound, C80 +8.4' only for white noise. On string music the hall is 5 dB over the dry sound and C80 is +1.7 to +2.6 dB. The renderer prints and documents numbers the file does not meet, it disagrees with the piano engine it says it matches, and it costs the counterpoint.
defects.evidence: hall_sk_final_wet-4.json: the IR's octave gain re flat is +10.6 dB at 125 Hz, +9.0 at 500 Hz, +3.0 at 4 kHz and -2.1 at 8 kHz, so reverb re dry per octave is +6.6/+5.5/+5.0/+3.7/+0.4/-1.0/-6.1 dB (125 Hz to 8 kHz). Weighted by the ricercar's own spectrum: reverb +5.0 dB re dry, C80 +1.7 dB (ISO 500-2k +2.6), while the renderer prints C80 +8.4. mix_sk_final.json measures the convolved program directly: reverb +4.4 dB, C80 +2.5 (fugue +4.1/+2.7). render_piano.py already calibrates --wet-db on the piano's long-term spectrum (hall_gain_on_piano_db, default 0 dB, C80 +4.9 measured on the render); the strings README claims the same default as the piano. clarity_sk_final.json: the new pitch dominates the previous note's partials 0.25 s into the note in 70.5/80/76% of changes in the mix (<0.5 s, 0.5-1 s, >=1 s) vs 92.6/94.5/92% in the dry sum; viola 68%. mix_fugue.json: fugue 16ths 50.5% in the mix vs 91.4% dry sum (63.4% at --wet -8). Round 1's 78% counted partials the two notes share; with those excluded it is 50%.
defects.fix: Port the piano's approach to hall.py/render_quartet.py. Compute the IR's gain on the quartet's long-term spectrum (octave-band energy of the four dry stems, or an LTAS stored at build time), set --wet against it so it is hall energy re dry on this music, and report hall_re_dry and C80 measured on the render (as hall_program_stats does) instead of the white-noise figure. Choose the default for the ensemble with the piano: the piano's 0 dB gives about C80 +4-5 here, and the current IR at --wet -8 measures ISO C80 +5.1 / program +3.8. Update the README's C80, 78% and 'same default as piano' claims.

defects.issue: The renderer's layer home-range floors, CC1 71 (mf) and 110 (ff), are still inside the SFZ crossfades (xfout 65-72 / 104-111), so two recordings still mix there. The renderer parks there often.
defects.evidence: held_sk_final.json, direct sfizz control: wander at CC1 71 is 2.06-3.53 dB vs 0.38-3.3 dB at 88 on the same keys, and at 110 it is 1.69-3.91 dB vs 0.62-1.85 dB at 114 (per-key excess up to +1.8 and +2.7 dB). CC1 104 is clean (within 0.14 dB of 88). Test-music A/B (sfizz on the kept job MIDIs, 71->72 and 110->111): +0.57 dB median, +2.11 dB max excess on 7 vn1 notes and +1.1 dB on 1 vn2 note. The job MIDIs send CC1 71 for 22.5 of vn1's 201.6 sounding seconds (its most used value) plus 7.6 s at 110; cello 11.9 s at 71. Part B's renderer notes at CC1 69/108 are clean because hysteresis plays them at 65/104, so they do not test 71/110.
defects.fix: Set LAYER_HOME mf=(72,104) and ff=(111,127) in iowa_build.py (or end the SFZ fades at 71/110: xfout_hicc1=71/110, xfin_hicc1=71/110), keeping LAYER_UP/LAYER_DOWN hysteresis consistent. Re-run an_held.py parts C/D; 71/110 should match 88/114 within 0.3 dB.

defects.issue: sfizz makes one-sample waveform slips on 256-sample block boundaries 10-20 ms into some notes, which show as isolated HF ticks in the dry stems.
defects.evidence: clickcause_sk_final.json: 12 of 19 flagged note-start spikes (vn2 5, va 6, vc 1) sit at position 0/255 of the render's 256-sample block grid. They are not in the source samples at the mapped position (7-12 dB vs 20-22 dB above the HF RMS), and they disappear when the same job MIDI is rendered with another block alignment (second-difference outlier 11.9x -> 4.3x at vn2 12.961 s; renders otherwise agree to -31..-42 dB). Level: -21 to -30 dB re the instrument's full-band level; 0 detections in the SK_final mix, 5 in the fugue mix at -25..-30 dB. The other 7 flags are the recordings' own bow noise.
defects.fix: Workaround: after sfizz, replace samples whose second difference exceeds 6x the local median at n%256 in {0,255} within 30 ms after a note start with cubic interpolation. Alternatively make the render shift a whole number of blocks and snap note-ons to the block grid if that removes the slip. Report the minimal repro (j2_vn2.mid rendered with a 0.5 s vs 0 s shift) upstream to sfizz.

defects.issue: Several key x layer combinations are 6-10 cents off, audibly and consistently. The worst is violin I Db5, flat on every occurrence in the test music.
defects.evidence: chain_sk_final.json: soprano Db5 (73) -7.0..-9.4 c by both estimators on all 6 long occurrences; alto Bb3 (58) +8.7 c, E4 (64) +6.2..+7.7 c. Soprano p95 6.2 c, 11 notes over 5 c; alto 7 over 5 c; none over 10 c. ladder.json: 22 key x layer over 5 c (max va ff C6 -9.7 c, vn1 ff F6 -8.2 c, vn1 mf Db5 -6.5 c). setup's closed loop only gates at 15 c.
defects.fix: Tighten the iowa_build.py --retune / verify_tuning.py gate from 15 c to 3-5 c for keys inside each compass (median over the steady part, both estimators), iterate the existing closed loop until it passes, and re-run an_ladder.py.

defects.issue: Violin I and II in unison on G3-D4 (keys 53-62) and on 82, 87 and 93-100 play the identical recording, so a unison is one violin 6 dB louder with no ensemble chorus.
defects.evidence: edge.json unison: C4 and G3 waveform correlation 1.00, sum +3.0 dB above the energy sum (fully coherent); A4/E5, which use different recordings, beat naturally (corr 0.25/0.01). violin2.sfz shares the Iowa source for 53-62, 82, 87 and 93-100. SK_final is not affected: its 2 unisons (F4, C5) use vn2's own recordings.
defects.fix: For shared keys, give violin2.sfz a decorrelated variant: the neighbouring key's recording transposed by one semitone, or the same recording with a different offset/loop phase plus a fixed +4-5 c detune and a mild body-EQ difference.

defects.issue: A key re-struck before its own note-off in the same voice is cut off at the first note-off, because sfizz releases every voice of the key.
defects.evidence: edge.json overlap: notes 72 at 0.5-1.5 s and 72 at 1.0-3.0 s; the second should sound until 3.0 s but is -38.7 dB at 2.0 s and -83 dB at 2.5 s. perform.py never writes this; it matters only for other MIDI sources.
defects.fix: When building a job, end a note 12 ms before the next note-on of the same key in that job (the existing repeated-key logic), so each sfizz note-off matches one voice.

qa.measurements:
All results are committed under /Users/biobook/Music/llm-music/fugue-jp/ricercar/audio/strings/qa/round2/results/. New this session: chain_sk_final.json, chain_sk_final_bd.json, bassdouble_sk_final_bd.json, mix_sk_final.json, held_sk_final.json, samples_shape.json, hall_sk_final_wet-4.json, hall_sk_final_wet-8.json, clarity_sk_final.json, clickcause_sk_final.json, loop_long.json. Kept from the interrupted run (its state hashes match the current render_quartet.py b32c34e0, perform.py 4d527a26 and all five SFZ): dyn.json, edge.json, ladder.json, setup.json, chain_fugue*.json, mix_fugue.json. Harness changes: an_mix.py's --hall none / --wet -8 comparison was hard-wired to the old fugue and now follows --tag; an_chain.py no longer crashes on the --bass-double job; new scripts an_held.py, an_samples.py, an_hall.py, an_clarity.py, an_clickcause.py, an_bassdouble.py, an_loop.py. Commits 4ac959e..390d868; no audio committed.

Test music is SK_final.ly + plan.json, 229 s. It has no notes under 0.26 s, so the short-stroke path is only covered by the old fugue.

Chain: 631/631 notes accounted, none dropped, stuck, hanging or transposed; the same with --bass-double auto (10 of 128 cello notes doubled, in tune within 3 c, about 5.9 dB under the cello). Pitch p95 (FFT / YIN): soprano 6.2/5.7 c, alto 4.3/4.6, tenor 2.5/2.6, bass 2.5/2.6; none over 10 c. Slur hand-over median +12.5 ms (93% within 20 ms). New bow after a rest reaches -6 dB at +19.6 ms median (p90 44 ms). 167 repeated keys dip 18 dB median (range 9-27 dB).

Round-1 interference fix: it holds. The renderer never parks strictly inside 66-70 / 105-109 (longest stay 0.26 s; 0.5-2.3 s total per instrument, all switch ramps). Held 6 s notes at CC1 49-114 through the renderer wander exactly like the single layer they play (max excess 0.2 dB). Parked inside a zone, sfizz alone still swells 3.8-5.5 dB median (max 6.55) vs 1.1-1.8 dB at the anchors, so the measure can detect the defect. A layer switch inside a held note costs 1.7-2.8 dB (dyn.json). The residual leak at CC1 71/110 is listed above.

Loop seams (20 s notes): the level step at every seam is within 0.4 dB, and no gated clicks.

Final file (SK_final): 48 kHz / 24-bit / 2 ch; -1.00 dBTP (m4a decoded -1.01, AAC 258 kb/s, aligned to 0 ms); no clipping; DC -110/-114 dB; -17.7 LUFS, LRA 19.5; lead-in digital silence. The tail fades 1.87 s after the last lift, at -74 dB re peak. K-weighted balance medians re the loudest: vn1 -1.2, vn2 -2.5, va -1.7, vc -0.8 dB. vn2's lower level follows the plan: the alto has 4 subject/answer roles vs the soprano's 7. L/R balance -1.5 dB, correlation 0.49. Mix clicks: 0.

Dynamics (dyn.json): pp->ff +20 to +22.7 dB; centroid ratio 1.23-1.80; gain-matched 2-5 kHz or 5-10 kHz +6.8 to +13.8 dB; role_level lifts vn2 2.9 dB.

Not defects: the 15 octave flags are weak fundamentals already present in the source samples (odd/even -7 to -21 dB, no sub-octave energy, both pitch estimators agree). The 3 'undetected' onsets and the one missing switch are octave slurs (all partials shared; switch 57-60 ms). The 140-400 ms old-partial falls have normal switch times (2.5-12.5 ms). The vc zipper figure is its 65 Hz fundamental inside the 10-100 Hz band. The vn2 D4 and va Gb3 wobbles at 2.4-5 Hz are the recordings' own amplitude vibrato.

Needed changes to perform.py or the piano renderer: none.

Disk: free space fell to 3.2 GB during the run because other agents are writing. I deleted this QA's own scratch audio and render temp directories (about 4.5 GB); about 10 GB was free at the end.
